Subject: Private offer flexibility — term length & buyer approval flow

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — we ran it by our cloud and security teams and the product looks promising. A couple procurement items came up we need to resolve before our CFO signs off:

- Term: our procurement team prefers an 18-month PO (matches budgeting cadence). Your standard is 12 months — are you able to support 18mo for a private offer?
- Pricing: we'll need clarity on discount tiers for multi-year or upfront payment.
- Approvals: what exact evidence do you need so our Legal and InfoSec can clear vendor risk quickly? Who signs first (procurement vs finance) and can we stage activation if legal needs more time?

I attached our internal procurement_form.pdf for your intake. Can you send a proposed MA P / PO structure and next steps? We hope to lock by end of month if possible.

Best,

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear summary and the form (received). Great to hear the demo resonated.

Short answer: we can support an 18-month private offer, but the commercial terms shift depending on payment cadence and evidence. High-level options I can propose quickly:

- 12-month standard PO: baseline list price, standard activation window (30 days).
- 18-month private offer: eligible for a one-time discount (we typically cap at ~10% on committed spend) if payment is annual or upfront.
- Staged activation: we can gate full access on completion of evidence items (SOC 2 summary, deployment diagram, contract countersign) and open core features for a technical pilot while legal finishes review.

To keep momentum, looping in Karthik (legal) to confirm acceptable contract language/approval windows and Vanessa for co-sell/partner incentives.

Can you share expected committed ARR (ballpark) and whether NovusHealth expects a co-sell motion with AWS (we can route through partner channels if so)? I’ll draft a private-offer PO and an evidence checklist and get that over within 48 hours.

Thanks,

Kimberly / Vanessa — quick legal take after reviewing procurement_form.pdf and our standard private-offer terms: 

1) Term length: 18 months is fine. We need to lock "term" as the contractual commitment period and ensure the invoice/payment cadence is explicit.
2) Discount cap: legal + finance prefer discount <= 10% on committed ARR for private offers to avoid margin erosion in resale channels. If Sales wants to stretch beyond 10% we need a documented approval (VP Sales sign-off).
3) Evidence & gating: require SOC2 Type II report summary, security-contact SLA, and an indemnity/limitation carve-out review if Novus requests changes. We can support staged activation (technical sandbox first, production upon countersign).
4) Approver flow: procurement initiates, finance (CFO) signs for payment terms; legal can provide conditional countersign and set a go-live hold. Recommend adding a short "mutual action plan" in the PO that lists the evidence items and timelines.

I can redline the PO draft — suggest we keep a single PO with an appendix for evidence and activation gating. If Sales wants to offer an extra concession (e.g., month 1 free, or expanded discount) route it through me and capture approval.

Karthik
Sr. Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Hi Sara / Procurement team — following internal review here is a proposed mutual action plan and next steps so we can accelerate to signature: 

Proposed commercial structure (NovusHealth private offer)
- Term: 18 months
- Committed ARR: $420,000 annual run-rate (please confirm)
- Pricing: 8% discount for annual invoicing; 10% discount for upfront payment (one-time invoice at execution)
- Activation: sandbox access within 5 business days after countersign; full production enabled within 3 business days of evidence acceptance.

Required evidence to clear InfoSec / Procurement (we attached a checklist):
- SOC 2 Type II summary or AICPA bridge document
- Deployment diagram showing data flows and region (must match us regions)
- Data retention & deletion policy summary
- Contact details for security/incident response

Next steps (suggested)
1) Procurement confirms committed ARR figure and preferred payment cadence.
2) We update the PO with the agreed discount and add the evidence appendix.
3) We route the private-offer DocuSign link to your Procurement and CFO (Mike Conrad).
4) Tech pilot can start under sandbox while legal finishes review.

I attached an evidence_checklist.xlsx to make the procurement intake easier. I'll also push a HubSpot deal update and a DocuSign envelope (link below) — please confirm stakeholders we should route to for signature.
